title: Points to Remember
weightage: Editorial selection; no verified exam frequency
gist: A one-liner becomes easier to remember when you attach its category, place and date. Start with these anchor facts, then use the source Q&A bank to build your own three-column revision sheet.

title: National Affairs
weightage: Editorial selection; no verified exam frequency
gist: Read national news as a chain: institution → decision → intended effect → number or date. Separate the historical launch of a scheme from a later expansion, and a legal right from its safeguards.

title: International Affairs
weightage: Editorial selection; no verified exam frequency
gist: International affairs is a matching exercise with a reason behind each match. Learn the organisation's members and purpose, then attach a summit's host, theme and outcome. Keep an index's edition year separate from the year it is released.

title: Economic Affairs
weightage: Editorial selection; no verified exam frequency
gist: Economic numbers need labels. Before learning a percentage, ask: GDP or GSDP, real or nominal, which financial year, and provisional estimate or budget estimate? Approval of a transaction is also different from its completion.

title: Science & Technology Affairs
weightage: Editorial selection; no verified exam frequency
gist: Make each technology story answer four questions: who built it, what it does, how it works, and what stage it reached. A flyby is different from a landing, and reactor criticality is different from commercial operation.

title: Environmental Affairs
weightage: Editorial selection; no verified exam frequency
gist: Environmental reports are easiest to read by separating a measured value, a target and a projection. Always preserve the baseline year, the unit and exclusions. For wetlands, keep the place-state pair and treat the issue's changing tally as dated information.

title: Uttar Pradesh Current Affairs
weightage: Editorial selection; no verified exam frequency
gist: Make a UP map in your head: event → district → purpose. Read the state budget separately from the economic survey: a budget proposes future spending, while the survey describes estimates and trends for earlier years.

title: Bihar Current Affairs
weightage: Editorial selection; no verified exam frequency
gist: Bihar remains in the supplied book even for a UPPSC reader. Use it for State-to-State comparisons, but keep proposed investments, July draft incentives and actual budget figures in separate boxes.

title: Short News, Awards and Persons
weightage: Editorial selection; no verified exam frequency
gist: Short news is best learned in pairs: person-post, book-author, exercise-partner and day-theme. Keep only one kind of pair on each flashcard so neighbouring table rows do not get mixed.

title: Sports News
weightage: Editorial selection; no verified exam frequency
gist: Start every sports note with the competition, edition and category. Men's and women's tournaments, T20 and ODI formats, and winners versus individual awards are different rows. Use the issue's result tables as dated source claims.
